question: In ruminants like cattle, bacteria present in ________ helps in digestion of cellulose.
solution:
The correct answer is __**rumen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In ruminants like cattle, bacteria present in the rumen (the largest compartment of the stomach) play a crucial role in the digestion of cellulose.
 
• The rumen is a fermentation chamber where complex carbohydrates, such as cellulose from plant material, are broken down by microbial fermentation.
 
• Bacteria in the rumen possess cellulolytic enzymes that break down cellulose into simpler forms that can be further digested and utilized by the ruminant host.
 
• This symbiotic relationship between ruminants and rumen bacteria allows them to efficiently extract nutrients from plant-based diets.

 Bacteria
 Use/Function
 
 
 
 

 Escherichia coli (E. coli)
 Used in molecular biology and biotechnology research
 
 

 
 Can produce recombinant proteins and enzymes
 
 

 Lactobacillus
 Used in the production of yogurt, cheese, and other dairy products
 
 

 
 Helps in the fermentation of vegetables and pickles
 
 

 Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt)
 Used as a biological pesticide against insect pests
 
 

 
 Produces insecticidal toxins targeting specific pests
 
 

 Streptococcus pneumoniae
 Can cause pneumonia and other respiratory infections
 
 

 
 Important in vaccine development against pneumonia
 
 

 Rhizobium
 Forms symbiotic relationships with leguminous plants
 
 

 
 Fixes atmospheric nitrogen, enhancing plant growth
 
 

 Saccharomyces cerevisiae (yeast)
 Used in baking, brewing, and fermentation processes
 
 

 
 Produces carbon dioxide and alcohol during fermentation
 
 

 Clostridium botulinum
 Produces botulinum toxin, used medically and in cosmetic procedures
 
 

 
 Causes botulism, a severe form of food poisoning
 
 

 Mycobacterium tuberculosis
 Causes tuberculosis (a bacterial infection) in humans
 
 

 
 Studied for developing diagnostic tests and treatments
 
 

 Pseudomonas aeruginosa
 Can cause infections in humans, particularly in immunocompromised individuals
 
 

 
 Used in bioremediation to degrade environmental pollutants
 
 

 Streptomyces
 Source of many antibiotics, such as streptomycin
 
 

 
 Used in the production of antibiotics and antifungal drugs
 
 

 Lactobacillus acidophilus
 Considered a probiotic bacterium, promotes gut health
 
 

 
 Aids in digestion and maintains a healthy intestinal flora
 
 

 Nitrosomonas
 Converts ammonia to nitrite in the nitrogen cycle
 
 

 
 Plays a role in the nitrification process in soil
 
 

 Helicobacter pylori
 Causes stomach ulcers and gastric infections
 
 

 
 Studied for understanding the pathogenesis of ulcers
